# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-10

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely strong — I know what Carnot does in one sentence, I see
`pip install carnot-ebm`, and the "47 + 28 = 76" example lands instantly. But
the moment I scroll to "Evidence" to decide whether to trust it, I hit a SOTA
35B model scoring **0%** on HumanEval, a baseline AUC of **0.125** (worse than a
coin flip), and two perfect scores. A skeptic reads a 0% baseline as a broken
harness — and a broken baseline makes me distrust every other number on the
page. The hero buys ten seconds; the results section spends them.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Implausible/too-perfect numbers in "Evidence" — "0% → 36%" on a 35B model,
   "0.90 AUC vs 0.125 baseline", "0.5 → 1.0", "60/60" — read as broken
   measurements and torch the page's credibility.
2. Vanity top-line stats — "382 Completed milestones", "3,304 Experiment runs",
   "30,658 Automated tests" are internal-process counters that tell a stranger
   nothing about whether the tool works; the one meaningful stat (AUROC) is the
   least prominent of the four.
3. Result cards are written in internal shorthand — "IterativeSelfRepair",
   "EstimationVerifier SVAMP", "VeriCoT", "CCTU", "HalluGuard v3",
   "PRM-BiasBench", "(paper-v6)" — a stranger can't parse the evidence and bounces.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Honest finding: the mechanical caps are mostly MET. No bento card exceeds
  ~120 words (longest, "Why Energy-Based?", ~75w); result-card bodies are short;
  results-grid has 12 cards and the blog has 7 (both under the ~20 ceiling).
  This page's problem is NOT classic word-count bloat.
- Structural exception — hero `stats-bar` (lines 304–314): a full "Recent
  progress" r-card is wedged in among the four stat numbers, so the headline row
  is four big numbers + one bordered paragraph card in the same flex strip. It
  reads as a crowded, half-finished header rather than a clean stats bar.
- Structural exception — features grid: the "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM"
  card (lines 495–501) sits OUTSIDE the closed `bento-grid` (`</div>` at line
  494), so it renders detached/misaligned below the seven-card grid.

### Internal jargon
- Hero "Recent progress" card — "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only
  0.8947", "Repinned from v2 0.9857", "pre-submission adversarial audit" — a
  stranger has no idea what "v2", "dual-condition", or "repinned" mean.
- Results section description — "synthetic-pilot … rows are labeled by
  provenance", "not model-generation headline claims" — defensive auditor copy,
  not landing-page copy.
- Result cards — "IterativeSelfRepair (HumanEval-50, execute-feedback-retry)",
  "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC", "FoVer baseline", "VeriCoT equation-style CoT
  fix", "GSM8K extraction TP rate", "PRM-BiasBench-style attacks", "k=5
  ensemble", "HalluGuard v3", "0.0pp accuracy delta", "CCTU" — these are class
  names, milestone-version names, and unexplained benchmark acronyms.
- Features — "PREM (Process-Reward Energy Model)", "Test-Time Compute (TTC)",
  "intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning", "AND-composed",
  "VerdictRecord", "SessionMemory" — the TTC/PREM card in particular is pure
  jargon with a grandiose tail and explains nothing to a non-insider.
- Preprint heading — "Carnot position paper (paper-v6)" and "pending
  operator-initiated upload" — "(paper-v6)" and "operator" are internal terms.

### Per-milestone narrative
- No raw `.NNN` milestone strings remain (good), but version-stamped internal
  names act as the same insider signal: "HalluGuard v3", "IterativeSelfRepair",
  "Repinned from v2 0.9857", "(paper-v6)". "pending operator-initiated upload"
  reads like a copied status line, not public copy.

### Inconsistencies
- THREE HumanEval numbers that don't reconcile on a skim: Code capability card
  says repair is "+3 points"; results card says "8% → 80% (+72pp)"
  (HumanEval-50); results card says "0% → 36%" (35B). A stranger can't tell if
  repair is worth 3 points or 72.
- The 47+28 example uses two different wrong answers: the intro and the
  "Whole-answer check" card say "= 76"; the "One-word-at-a-time" card (line 338)
  says "= 7". Pick one.
- Four 0.9x figures for three different things: hero stat 0.9131 (FoVer), hero
  card's repin from 0.9857, results "0.91 AUROC (publication gate)" for
  prompt-injection, and "0.90 AUC" (SVAMP). The identical-looking numbers for
  unrelated tasks invite confusion.
- Meter bar widths don't map to the numbers: "+3.0 points" → 14.6% width but
  "+4.9 points" → 66.7% width. Decorative bars that contradict the cited values
  undercut the section's own "every number is backed" promise.

### Missing essentials
- WHO maintains it: only "© 2026 Ian Blenke" in the footer. With "382
  milestones / 3,304 runs / autonomous research loop," a stranger may read this
  as one person + an AI loop churning artifacts, not a credible lab. No
  About/team/affiliation/funding line.
- WHY trust the numbers: the page asserts trust (artifact-backed, provenance
  labels) but shows none externally — no leaderboard, third-party eval, or
  reproduction link. The defensive disclaimer plus the implausible numbers makes
  the trust case weaker, not stronger.
- Present and good: one-sentence "what is it" (hero), install command, Apache 2.0.

### Fabrication signals
- "SOTA 35B (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) — HumanEval pass@1: 0% → 36%": a 35B SOTA model
  scoring 0% baseline on HumanEval is not credible (such models score ~70%+).
  Reads as a broken harness and poisons the "+36%" alongside it.
- "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)": AUC 0.125 is far below random (0.5);
  using a below-random baseline to inflate the delta is a red flag.
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0": a perfect 1.0.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks": 100% on n=60 with no credibility anchor.
- "99.3% of wrong code flagged": very high; it IS anchored to 164-problem
  HumanEval so it's the least suspicious, but it still reads as eye-catching.
- Compounding irony a stranger will feel: the blog row is dominated by "Caught
  Cheating", "Two Retractions and a Rescue", "Regex in an NTK Costume", "Five
  FATAL Findings" — the project advertises catching ITSELF fabricating, then
  presents perfect/implausible numbers on the same page. That juxtaposition
  amplifies doubt rather than resolving it.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero is excellent: crisp one-line value prop, a concrete 47+28 example a
  non-expert gets immediately, and install + license + mirror all above the fold.
- "How it works" (Extract → Check → Repair) is clear, low-jargon, and honest
  ("we use patterns and a second small LLM pass"). The visual design is clean
  and professional.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
- Fix the two layout bugs: lift the "Recent progress" r-card out of the hero

- Triage Evidence for credibility before anything else: drop or heavily caveat

- De-jargon every result-card tag: replace internal class/benchmark names with
  plain descriptions ("Code repair on 50 HumanEval problems", "Math word

- Replace the vanity stats: drop "382 milestones / 3,304 runs / 30,658 tests"

- Reconcile the three HumanEval claims into one clearly-scoped number; fix the

- Add a one-line maintainer/affiliation/About so the page doesn't read as a solo
